title: How HNSW Vector Search Works
youtubeTitle: How Vector Search Works in Milliseconds ⚡ #Shorts
youtubeDescription: Understand how Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) graphs index dense vector embeddings to achieve sub-millisecond similarity search.

scenes.visualBody: Brute force cosine distance compares against millions of points linearly, collapsing search throughput.
scenes.voiceText: Searching millions of high-dimensional vectors linearly creates an unscalable bottleneck for AI applications.

scenes.visualBody: Top layers make massive express leaps while base layers pinpoint exact nearest neighbors.
scenes.voiceText: Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs skip dense clusters like multi-tier highways across high-dimensional space.

scenes.visualBody: Coarse hops converge rapidly down to the densest layer, reducing complexity from linear to logarithmic.
scenes.voiceText: The search hops across sparse upper layers before descending to the base for precise nearest neighbor convergence.

scenes.visualBody: Tune graph connectivity M and construction breadth efSearch to balance recall against memory footprint.
scenes.voiceText: Balancing graph connectivity with construction depth is how production vector databases maintain sub-millisecond latency.
